title: The Patents Act, 1970
summary: Primary Indian patent statute. Governs what can be patented, examination procedure, and opposition.

title: The Patents Act, 1970 — Section 3(p)
summary: Bars patenting an invention that is, in effect, traditional knowledge or an aggregation/duplication of known properties of traditionally known components. Courts have held this provides 'defensive protection' rather than a blanket ban on all TK-based inventions -- the analysis is fact-specific to how the claimed invention differs from the known traditional use.

title: Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL)
summary: Documented database of codified traditional medicine knowledge (Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani, Yoga) used by patent offices worldwide as prior art to prevent erroneous patenting of known traditional formulations.

title: The Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999
summary: Governs GI registration for products (including Ayurvedic formulations tied to a specific region) -- relevant where a product's identity is linked to geographic origin, e.g. a specific district's traditional preparation.

title: The Trade Marks Act, 1999
summary: Governs trademark registration for product/brand names -- separate from patent protection for the formulation itself.

title: The Designs Act, 2000
summary: Protects the visual/ornamental design of an article (e.g. distinctive packaging or container shape) as distinct from its functional formulation.

title: The Copyright Act, 1957
summary: Covers original literary/artistic works -- relevant to product labeling text, packaging artwork, and published research/documentation, not the formulation or method itself.

title: The Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001
summary: Governs registration and protection of new plant varieties, including medicinal plant cultivars used as raw material in Ayurvedic formulations.

title: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002
version: as amended by the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023 (in force from 1 April 2024)
summary: Establishes India's Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) framework for use of biological resources and associated knowledge. Requires prior approval from the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) before filing IP applications based on biological resources obtained from India.

title: Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023 — amended Section 7
summary: Exempts registered AYUSH practitioners, local communities, growers/cultivators of biodiversity, and users of codified traditional knowledge from the requirement to give prior intimation to the State Biodiversity Board when accessing biological resources for commercial use -- provided a Certificate of Origin is obtained from the local Biodiversity Management Committee for cultivated medicinal plants.

title: The Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Rules, 1945
summary: Governs licensing, manufacture and classification of Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani (ASU) drugs -- distinguishes classical/generic formulations (drawn from recognized authoritative texts) from patent-or-proprietary and new ASU drug categories, each with different approval requirements.

title: The Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954
summary: Restricts advertisements claiming a drug/remedy can cure specific listed diseases -- relevant to marketing claims made about an Ayurvedic product.

title: FSSAI Ayurveda Aahar Regulations
summary: Defines a distinct 'Ayurveda Aahar' food category for products based on traditional Ayurvedic dietary concepts -- relevant when classifying a product as food/nutraceutical rather than a drug.

title: IP India — Patents, Trademarks, Designs & GI Registry (InPASS)
summary: Official Indian IP office portal and public search databases for patents (InPASS), trademarks, designs and GI registrations -- primary source for checking existing registrations and filing status.

title: TRIPS Agreement (Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights)
summary: WTO agreement setting minimum global standards for IP protection that member countries (including India) must implement domestically.

title: Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)
summary: International treaty establishing state sovereignty over biological resources and the principle of fair and equitable benefit-sharing -- the international legal basis underlying India's Biological Diversity Act.

title: Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit-Sharing
summary: Supplementary agreement to the CBD implementing detailed Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) obligations -- relevant when an Ayurvedic product involves cross-border use of genetic resources or associated traditional knowledge.

title: WIPO Treaty on Intellectual Property, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge (GRATK)
version: adopted 24 May 2024; enters into force 3 months after 15 ratifications
summary: First WIPO treaty addressing IP, genetic resources and traditional knowledge. Once in force, requires patent applicants whose claimed invention is 'based on' genetic resources or associated traditional knowledge to disclose the country of origin or the Indigenous Peoples/local community that provided it. Directly relevant to any foreign patent filing built on Ayurvedic traditional knowledge.

title: Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT)
summary: Allows filing a single international patent application that can later be pursued in multiple member countries -- the standard route for seeking patent protection outside India.

title: Madrid System for the International Registration of Marks
summary: Single-application system for registering a trademark across multiple member countries -- relevant for protecting an Ayurvedic brand name internationally.

title: Hague System for the International Registration of Industrial Designs
summary: Single-application system for registering industrial designs (e.g. packaging) across multiple member countries.

title: Budapest Treaty on the International Recognition of the Deposit of Microorganisms
summary: Governs deposit of microorganisms for patent purposes -- relevant if an Ayurvedic/fermentation-based formulation's patent application requires a biological deposit.

title: EU Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 — Article 4 (Responsible Person)
legal_instrument: Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council
summary: Article 4 mandates that only cosmetic products for which a legal or natural person is designated within the Community as 'Responsible Person' shall be placed on the market. The Responsible Person shall ensure compliance with each cosmetic product's safety, GMP, PIF, CPNP notification, and SUE obligations.

title: EU Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 — Article 10 (Safety Assessment & CPSR)
authority: European Commission / Scientific Committee on Consumer Safety (SCCS)
legal_instrument: Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council
summary: Article 10 mandates that prior to placing a cosmetic product on the market, the Responsible Person shall ensure that the product has undergone a safety assessment on the basis of relevant information and that a Cosmetic Product Safety Report (CPSR) is drawn up in accordance with Annex I by a qualified safety assessor holding a recognized diploma in pharmacy, toxicology, medicine or similar discipline.

title: EU Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 — Article 11 (Product Information File - PIF)
authority: European Commission / Member State Competent Authorities
legal_instrument: Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council
summary: Article 11 requires the Responsible Person to keep a Product Information File (PIF) readily accessible in electronic or other format at the address specified on the label for a period of 10 years following the date on which the last batch was placed on the market. The PIF must contain the description of the cosmetic product, CPSR, manufacturing method conforming to ISO 22716 GMP, proof of claimed effects, and data on any animal testing.

title: EU Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 — Article 13 (CPNP Notification)
legal_instrument: Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council
summary: Article 13 dictates that prior to placing a cosmetic product on the market, the Responsible Person shall submit electronically to the European Commission via CPNP: product category and name, RP name and address, country of origin, Member State of first placing on market, presence of nanomaterials, and frame formulation for prompt medical treatment.

title: EU Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 — Article 16 (Nanomaterials)
legal_instrument: Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council
summary: Article 16 establishes that cosmetic products containing nanomaterials must be notified to the Commission electronically by the Responsible Person 6 months prior to placing on the market (except for colorants, preservatives, and UV filters listed in Annexes IV to VI). Notification must include identification, specifications, toxicological profile, and exposure conditions.

title: EU Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 — Article 23 (Communication of Serious Undesirable Effects - SUE)
authority: Member State Competent Authorities / European Commission
legal_instrument: Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council
summary: Article 23 governs cosmetovigilance, requiring that in the event of Serious Undesirable Effects (SUE), the Responsible Person and distributors shall without delay notify the competent authority of the Member State where the SUE occurred, detailing the type of SUE, product name, and corrective measures taken.

title: EU Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 — Annex I (Cosmetic Product Safety Report - CPSR)
subdomain: CPSR Part A & Part B Structure
summary: Annex I establishes the mandatory structure of the Cosmetic Product Safety Report (CPSR): Part A (Cosmetic Product Safety Information: quantitative formula, physical/chemical characteristics, stability, microbiological quality, impurities, packaging, normal and foreseeable use, exposure to the product/substances, toxicological profile) and Part B (Cosmetic Product Safety Assessment: assessment conclusion, labeled warnings and instructions of use, scientific reasoning, and safety assessor's credentials).
